name: TN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 partisan lean in a Knoxville-area district Republicans have held for years
Incumbent Tim Burchett's large fundraising edge ($2.4M raised vs. $398K for Michaela Barnett)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; the Democratic challenger has modest cash on hand
model.rationale: An R+17 district with a well-funded incumbent running for renomination leaves little basis for expecting competition, and prediction markets price the Republican near 95 percent; fundraising disparities reinforce the structural advantage.
model.watch: Any polling showing Burchett below fifty percent, or significant outside spending against him, would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Burchett seeks another term in a Knoxville-area district that leans Republican by about seventeen points at the presidential level. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $2.4 million to Michaela Barnett's roughly $400,000, and carries the incumbency in a seat Republicans have held for years. Two independents also appear on the ballot but show no measurable campaign activity.

No public polling or expert ratings are available for this race, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which price Republican chances around 95 percent. The district's strong partisan lean makes an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin. A Democratic win would require a dramatic, district-specific shift well beyond anything visible in the current evidence.
